title: Certificate name matching
description:
Write the hostname check every TLS client performs (lesson 3.05):

```cpp
bool nameMatches(const std::string& certificateName, const std::string& host);
bool certificateMatches(const std::vector<std::string>& names, const std::string& host);
```

- **nameMatches** compares ignoring case. A trailing dot on either side is ignored (`example.com.`).
  - A name without `*` matches only the same host.
  - A wildcard is allowed **only** as the whole leftmost label (`*.example.com`). It matches exactly one non-empty label in that position: `a.example.com` yes; `example.com` and `a.b.example.com` no.
  - Wildcards are refused (never match) if the rest of the name has fewer than two labels (`*.com`, `*`), and `*` anywhere else (`x*.example.com`, `a.*.example.com`) never matches.
  - A host that is an IPv4 address (four dot-separated numbers) never matches a wildcard.
- **certificateMatches** is true if any of the certificate's names matches.
hints: Split both names into labels. With a wildcard, the certificate's first label must be exactly `*`, no other label may contain `*`, both must have the same number of labels, and every label after the first must be equal.
